title: bee.mjs: guarded compile cache + lazy-import split for heavy single-consumer libs
action: Per exec-speed D1. (a) Add a guarded top-level compile-cache enable to .bee/bin/bee.mjs right after the existing node: imports: try { const { enableCompileCache } = await import('node:module'); if (typeof enableCompileCache === 'function') enableCompileCache(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bee-compile-cache')); } catch {} — fail-open, zero output. NOTE: ESM hoisting means this only benefits dynamically imported modules and spawned children; that is expected and documented in plan.md. (b) Lazy-import split: find static imports whose EVERY use site is inside handler function bodies (candidates: worktree-store.mjs, integration-queue.mjs, herding.mjs, feedback.mjs, workflow-store.mjs, schedule.mjs, scratch.mjs, perf-adjacent libs). For each such lib, remove the static import and add `const { ... } = await import('./lib/<name>.mjs');` at the top of each consuming handler (handlers are already async or can be made async — the dispatcher awaits handler() uniformly at the call site, verified at bee.mjs:8405). NEVER convert: any lib whose symbols are referenced at module top level, in parseFlags/resolveCommand/registry paths, or re-exported for tests. Behavior must stay byte-identical on stdout/stderr for every verb. Measure before/after: run `node .bee/bin/bee.mjs cells show --id es-1 --json` 3x and note the [bee] timing line deltas in your result message.
